narrative.overview:
This is an operator's dashboard reduced to signal. A French lycée student opens it several times a day to answer one question — what do I have to do next — so the interface earns its keep by getting out of the way. It is monochrome on purpose: near-black ink on paper white, a full ramp of cool slate greys, and almost nothing else. Colour is rationed so that when it appears — a red badge on an unfinished assignment, an amber pill on an assessment that is still coming, a single blue 'mark done' — it means something and reads instantly. Restraint is the feature, not a limitation.

The surface is flat and quiet at rest: cards are white (or near-black in dark mode) held by a one-pixel hairline, corners softened to 8px, no shadow. Rhythm is generous and consistent — a 1.5rem gap between the stacked sections of every page — while the content inside stays dense and scannable: 0.875rem is the workhorse size, tables and lists are tight, and hierarchy comes from weight and a Geist-Sans heading rather than scale jumps. Both themes are first-class and class-driven; the student toggles between them and the choice sticks.

The identity lives in the small, exact details — the pill geometry shared by every button and every status chip, the left-border accent on a timetable lesson, the persistent blue ring on a search result you jumped to — not in any decorative gesture. Nothing here is trying to impress; it is trying to be legible at a glance on a phone in a hallway between classes.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome slate-grey system; colour is semantic and rare.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, 8px card corners, fully-round buttons and chips.
0.875rem body / 0.75rem labels; dense content, roomy 1.5rem section rhythm.
Geist Sans for headings, system sans (Arial/Helvetica) for body, Geist Mono for code.
Dark and light are equal, .dark-class driven, user-toggled and persisted.
Touch-first: pill targets, max-w-6xl centered column, sm: is the primary breakpoint.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue is action and wayfinding only — the contextual primary button, links, the search-highlight ring, a lesson's default accent border. It is never a background wash, never decorative, and never competes with the black primary button for 'the main thing to click'.

rules.name: The Rationed Colour Rule
rules.body: On a resting screen, colour covers a few percent of the pixels — badges, chips, one or two links. If a new screen needs a colour block to work, the layout is wrong first.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by font-weight (400 body to 600 headings) and the Geist/Arial switch, not by a big type scale. Display is only 1.4x body. Keep new headings in this narrow range.

rules.name: The Geist-Heading Rule
rules.body: New headings (h1, h2 section titles) get font-sans (Geist). Body, labels and controls stay on the system stack. Geist Mono is for code / pasted JSON only. Implementation note: Geist is loaded via next/font and exposed as --font-geist-sans; existing headings do not yet carry font-sans — apply it on new work and when touching a heading.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest — hairline + tonal background only. A shadow means 'this element is floating above the page' (modal, dropdown), never 'this card is important'. Provisional: the owner is open to a single very soft resting shadow on primary cards later; if added, it becomes a named token and applies uniformly, not per-card.

dos: Do stack every page as flex flex-col gap-6 sections inside the max-w-6xl column.
Do hold surfaces with a 1px hairline (border-zinc-300 / dark:border-zinc-800) and the Canvas→Paper tonal step; keep them shadowless.
Do make every button and every status chip a full pill (rounded-full); use rounded-lg for cards and rounded for fields.
Do reserve bg-foreground (near-black pill) for the one primary action per view and bg-blue-600 for the one contextual 'do it now' action.
Do label fields with text-xs text-zinc-500 above the control, and keep body text at text-sm.
Do put Geist (font-sans) on new headings; leave body and controls on the system stack.
Do wrap fixed-width views (grids, calendars) in overflow-x-auto with a min-w-[…] inner track so the page never scrolls sideways.
Do ship every new surface in both themes, driven by the .dark class, with a real dark value for every colour used.
donts: Don't use blue as a background wash, a section fill, or decoration — it is action and wayfinding only (The One Blue Rule).
Don't add a resting shadow to a card to signal importance; a shadow means 'floating above the page'.
Don't build hierarchy with big type — stay inside the 1x–1.4x range and use weight plus the Geist/Arial switch (The Weight-Not-Size Rule).
Don't introduce a fifth hue. Neutrals carry structure; red/green/amber carry state; blue carries action. That is the whole palette.
Don't invent a new radius. Two values and a pill.
Don't rely on colour alone for a state — pair it with a letter, label or icon (the T/C badges, the status chips).
Don't add a 'current page' highlight to the nav unless it is designed system-wide; today the nav has none.
